intro_text.en: Concise syllabus coverage: Redis overview/setup; Strings, Lists, Sets and Hashes; basic commands; transactions; caching/TTL; AI use cases and simplified application integration. Includes eight real Redis examples for Practical 9, without advanced extras.

body.en:
Redis stores keys mapped to data structures, mainly served from memory. It is useful for caches, sessions, counters and simple queues. Persistence is configurable; do not assume a memory-first cache is a durable system of record.

Install using the official guide for your OS. Start a private, authenticated instance and connect with redis-cli. The usual port is 6379; use your actual settings. Keep passwords out of shared code and never expose Redis directly to public browsers.

redis-cli --user YOUR_USER --askpass PING
# Enter your private password; expected CLI reply: PONG

This unit covers 10 hours / 17%, CO5 and Practical 9: install Redis and practise Strings, Lists, Sets and Hashes. CLI snippets use practice keys on your own instance; the downloadable Python examples isolate and clean their own keys.

A String stores a byte/string value. Use SET/GET, INCR for an integer-formatted counter, EXISTS to test a key, TYPE to inspect its type and DEL to remove it. A missing GET returns nil/null; using the wrong structure command can raise WRONGTYPE.

SET lab:product 'Sensor Node'
GET lab:product
SET lab:views 10
INCR lab:views
TYPE lab:product
EXISTS lab:product
DEL lab:product

SET normally replaces the existing value. Redis hash field values and numeric-looking strings are not automatically Python numbers.

A List is ordered and allows duplicates. LPUSH/RPUSH add at the left/right; LPOP/RPOP remove from those ends. LRANGE 0 -1 reads the whole list. RPUSH plus LPOP gives a basic FIFO pattern, not a complete reliable job-processing system.

RPUSH lab:jobs train evaluate
LPUSH lab:jobs load
LRANGE lab:jobs 0 -1
LPOP lab:jobs

Here the list is load, train, evaluate; LPOP removes load.

A Set stores unique, unordered members. SADD adds, SMEMBERS reads, SISMEMBER tests membership and SREM removes. Adding Python twice does not create two members.

SADD lab:skills Python Redis Python
SMEMBERS lab:skills
SISMEMBER lab:skills Python
SREM lab:skills Redis

Suitable examples: unique skills, tags or visitor IDs. Display order is not guaranteed; the Python example sorts only for readable output.

A Hash stores field–value pairs under one key, for example a small user/profile record. HSET writes fields, HGET reads one, HGETALL reads all and HDEL removes fields.

HSET lab:user name Asha city Surat age 20
HGET lab:user name
HGETALL lab:user
HDEL lab:user age

The age value is stored/read as string "20" in these examples. Use a list for ordered items, a set for unique members and a hash for named fields.

MULTI queues commands; EXEC executes them together without another client’s command interleaving during execution. DISCARD cancels the queued work before execution.

MULTI
INCR lab:views
GET lab:views
EXEC
# DISCARD cancels queued commands before execution.

No rollback: an execution-time error does not undo successful commands, and later queued commands can still run. Program 6 demonstrates this with a non-integer INCR and a later successful write. The Python transaction pipeline uses MULTI/EXEC.

A cache hit finds the value; a miss requires the source. In cache-aside, the application reads Redis first, then loads and caches the source value on a miss.

SET lab:recs 'P101,P102' EX 60
GET lab:recs
TTL lab:recs
DEL lab:recs   # invalidate after a source-data change
  • TTL: limits lifetime. TTL returns seconds; -1 means no expiry and -2 means missing.
  • Invalidation: delete/update cached data when the authoritative value changes.
  • Other strategies: write-through updates cache with source writes; write-behind delays source writes and needs careful failure handling.

Expiry is not memory-pressure eviction. Caches may be stale or unavailable; keep a source fallback and do not claim unlimited memory, durability or guaranteed speedups.

h.en: 5.8 AI use cases and simplified application integration

body.en:
Redis can cache recommendation IDs, temporary feature values or sessions, and hold simple job lists. Storing these values does not train an AI model.

Integration: application → Redis; on a miss → source database/service → Redis with TTL → response. Use an official client such as Python redis-py. Version cache keys when the model/data meaning changes and protect personal data.

GET cache-key
# HIT: return the cached value.
# MISS: read the authoritative source, then
SET cache-key value EX 60

Program 8 really connects Python to Redis and shows source → cache → invalidation. Its source is a small local dictionary fixture, not a live MongoDB/Cassandra integration or benchmark. The reference uses Redis/CLI 8.10.3 and redis-py 8.1.0, privately on port 6385.

h.en: Install/connect and verify one stored round-trip.

body.en: Use your OS guide, private authentication and redis-cli PING. SET a disposable string, GET the same value, then DEL only that key.

h.en: Choose and practise the four structures.

body.en: String: product name/counter. List: ordered jobs. Set: unique skills. Hash: named user fields. Use the corresponding quick-reference commands.

h.en: Execute a small transaction and explain failure behaviour.

body.en: Use MULTI/EXEC (or the Python transaction pipeline). Program 6 returns [11,"11"]; a later example’s failed INCR does not prevent its subsequent SET. DISCARD cancels before execution.

h.en: Add expiry and invalidate a cached recommendation.

body.en: SET the result with EX 60, confirm TTL is active, read it as a hit, then DEL it on source change. TTL -2 confirms it is missing.

Run program 8: first read comes from the local source fixture; second from Redis. Update the fixture, invalidate, and read the new value. Record actual outputs; no trained model or live multi-database claim.

code.en:
from lab import Lab, show

with Lab('ns5p01',['product']) as lab:
    r=lab.r; k=lab.key('product')
    show('ping',r.ping())
    show('set',r.set(k,'Sensor Node'))
    show('get',r.get(k))
    show('exists',r.exists(k))
    show('type',r.type(k))
    show('deleted',r.delete(k))
    show('missing',r.get(k))

programs.out:
ping: true
set: true
get: "Sensor Node"
exists: 1
type: "string"
deleted: 1
missing: null

expl.en: Real stored round-trip. redis-py reports PING/SET success as true; redis-cli shows PONG/OK. Lab isolates and cleans declared keys.

code.en:
from lab import Lab, show

with Lab('ns5p02',['views','temporary']) as lab:
    r=lab.r; k=lab.key('views'); temp=lab.key('temporary')
    r.set(k,'10')
    show('incremented',r.incr(k))
    show('stored_string',r.get(k))
    r.set(temp,'cached',ex=60)
    show('ttl_active',0<r.ttl(temp)<=60)
    r.expire(temp,0)
    show('after_immediate_expiry',r.get(temp))
    show('missing_ttl',r.ttl(temp))

programs.out:
incremented: 11
stored_string: "11"
ttl_active: true
after_immediate_expiry: null
missing_ttl: -2

expl.en: INCR returns integer 11; GET reads string "11". SET EX adds a lifetime; EXPIRE 0 immediately expires the key. TTL -2 means missing.

code.en:
from lab import Lab, show

with Lab('ns5p03',['jobs']) as lab:
    r=lab.r; k=lab.key('jobs')
    r.rpush(k,'train','evaluate'); r.lpush(k,'load')
    show('jobs',r.lrange(k,0,-1))
    show('removed_left',r.lpop(k))
    show('remaining',r.lrange(k,0,-1))
    show('length',r.llen(k))

expl.en: Lists preserve order. These are job-name strings, not executed AI training or a reliable-worker implementation.

code.en:
from lab import Lab, show

with Lab('ns5p04',['skills']) as lab:
    r=lab.r; k=lab.key('skills')
    show('added',r.sadd(k,'Python','Redis','Python'))
    show('members',sorted(r.smembers(k)))
    show('has_python',r.sismember(k,'Python'))
    show('removed',r.srem(k,'Redis'))
    show('remaining',sorted(r.smembers(k)))

expl.en: Duplicate Python is stored once. Sorting is only for readable output; Redis set order is not guaranteed.

code.en:
from lab import Lab, show

with Lab('ns5p05',['user']) as lab:
    r=lab.r; k=lab.key('user')
    show('new_fields',r.hset(k,mapping={
        'name':'Asha','city':'Surat','age':'20'}))
    show('name',r.hget(k,'name'))
    show('profile',r.hgetall(k))
    show('removed_age',r.hdel(k,'age'))
    show('remaining',r.hgetall(k))

expl.en: A hash keeps named string fields under one key. The helper sorts map fields for stable display; it does not change stored values.

code.en:
from lab import Lab, show

with Lab('ns5p06',['count','after']) as lab:
    r=lab.r; k=lab.key('count'); after=lab.key('after')
    r.set(k,'10')
    with r.pipeline(transaction=True) as p:
        p.incr(k); p.get(k)
        show('exec',p.execute())
    r.set(k,'text')
    with r.pipeline(transaction=True) as p:
        p.incr(k); p.set(after,'done')
        show('exec_with_error',p.execute(raise_on_error=False))
    show('later_write',r.get(after))

programs.out:
exec: [11,"11"]
exec_with_error: [{"server_error":"value is not an integer or out of range"},true]
later_write: "done"

expl.en: The transaction pipeline uses MULTI/EXEC. A real non-integer INCR error does not stop the later SET; Redis does not roll back successful commands.

code.en:
from lab import Lab, show

with Lab('ns5p07',['recs:U42:v1']) as lab:
    r=lab.r; k=lab.key('recs:U42:v1')
    show('initial_miss',r.get(k))
    r.set(k,'P101,P102',ex=60)
    show('cache_hit',r.get(k))
    show('ttl_active',0<r.ttl(k)<=60)
    r.delete(k)
    show('after_invalidation',r.get(k))

programs.out:
initial_miss: null
cache_hit: "P101,P102"
ttl_active: true
after_invalidation: null

expl.en: Cache recommendation IDs under a versioned key with TTL. These fixed IDs are not output from a trained model; invalidation removes the cached copy.
Actual Python + Redis: miss → source fixture, hit → Redis, update/invalidate → new source value. The dictionary is not a live MongoDB/Cassandra service or a performance benchmark.

terms.en: Conceptual flow. Program 8 executes Python + Redis with a local source fixture; not a live multi-database deployment.

a.en: A memory-first data-structure server commonly used for caching, sessions, counters and simple queues.

q.en: Which four structures are required here?
Which commands store and read a string?

a.en: SET and GET. A missing GET returns nil/null.
A list is ordered and permits duplicates; a set holds unique members without guaranteed order.
Field–value pairs under one key, read/written with HGET/HSET and related commands.
A missing key or a value representing an integer; a non-integer stored string causes an error.

q.en: What do MULTI, EXEC and DISCARD do?

a.en: Queue commands, execute the queue, or cancel it before execution respectively.

q.en: Does a Redis transaction roll back runtime errors?

a.en: No. Successful commands are not undone and later queued commands can still execute.
-1: existing key without expiry. -2: missing key.
Read cache first; on a miss read the authoritative source and cache the result with a suitable lifetime.
To prevent serving an outdated value after the authoritative source changes.

q.en: Does this unit train AI or prove a live multi-database integration?

a.en: No. AI caching is an application use case; the executed integration is Python + Redis with a local dictionary source.
